chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sa'd, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'We deal with this 'inah [sale for credit] transaction, and sometimes a man comes to us seeking to sell, but he is not with us; so we bargain with him and agree on his price before we buy it from him. Then we buy the goods and sell them to him at that agreed price, neither increasing nor decreasing anything.' He said, 'There is no objection.'

key_terms.الْعِينَةَ: Inah: A specific type of sale used for credit transactions, often involving buying and selling the same item back.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: La ba'sa: There is no harm; it is permissible.
key_terms.نُقَاطِعُهُ: Nuqati'uhu: We agree/conclude a deal with him.

ai.seo_question: Is the 'inah sale transaction permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* validates the 'inah structure as a legitimate commercial practice rather than a mere legal fiction, provided the underlying sale is genuine. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms its permissibility, offering Shia jurists a basis for using this mechanism in credit transactions while maintaining the formal requirements of a valid sale (bay').
